title: Nitpicker analyzer report
description: Language-neutral output contract of a Nitpicker analyzer: an object with a findings array. Extracted from core/diff/comparison/finding-schema.mjs (parseAnalyzerReport / parseFinding). The reference implementation additionally normalizes path separators before applying the path rules below.

path.description: Git-style relative path that stays within the analyzed project: not absolute, no drive letter, no leading '..'.

identity.description: Stable identity used to match a finding between base and head snapshots.

classification.description: enforceable findings fail the gate when new; descriptive findings are report-only; tool-error findings mark an analyzer failure.

allowedForm.description: What to write instead, as the message states it: the sentence or sentences that name the accepted form of the code. It must be part of `message`; left out when the rule states none apart from the problem.

exception.description: The entry that accepts this finding when it is intended, as the message prints it. The engine fills it in from the sentence the message ends with (`If this is intended, add {...} to "exceptions" in nitpicker.config.json.`) when the analyzer leaves it out, and refuses one that differs from that sentence or that a message without the sentence carries. Its `reason` is a placeholder to replace.

exceptionList.description: The list of nitpicker.config.json that takes `exception`: `exceptions`, or `python.exceptions` for the Python rules the top-level list does not take.

policyKind.description: On a policy-loosened finding of a report: which kind of policy change it is, which picks the guidance its message gives.

tokens.description: The words of the message. A new finding of three or more tokens counts as already present when the base has an unmatched finding with the same tool, rule, path and classification, the same number of tokens and at most one differing token.

helpUri.description: Link to the page that explains the rule. Nitpicker fills it in new-findings.json from its rule reference (docs/rules); an analyzer may set its own.

exception.description: An entry of the `exceptions` list of nitpicker.config.json.

column.description: 1-based column in UTF-16 code units, a tab counting as one; adapters convert the columns of tools that count code points, UTF-8 bytes or tab stops.

ratchet.description: Lets an enforceable finding whose identity changed stay baselined: a new finding matching a base finding's ratchet key (with renames applied) is held while its value does not exceed the base value.

worseMessage.description: Message to report instead of `message` (with `worseAllowedForm` for `allowedForm`) when the finding is new only because its value grew past the base value; `{base}` is replaced with the base value.

worseAllowedForm.description: The `allowedForm` to report together with `worseMessage`; `{base}` is replaced with the base value.

growthAdvice.description: Text added to `message`, before its exception sentence, when the finding is new while the base already had findings under the same ratchet key; `{base}` is replaced with the base value.

growthAllowedForm.description: The part of `growthAdvice` that names the allowed form; it is appended to `allowedForm` when `growthAdvice` is added to `message`.

heldMessage.description: Message to report instead of `message` when the finding is held because its value did not exceed the base value; `{base}` is replaced with the base value.

existingCodeOnly.description: When true, a finding on a line the change added is never held by the ratchet or matched to the base by identity: the code it points at is new.

pathIsFolder.description: When true, `path` is a folder: a base finding with no match at its own path is held at the folder most of its files were renamed to.

folderFiles.description: With `pathIsFolder`: the number of files in the folder, when `value` is not that number. A base finding is held at a new path when more than half of these files were renamed there.

metric.description: Numeric measurement; only descriptive findings may carry one.
